assistant|business_trip_packing_list_clo: For a 3-day business trip, recommended 2-3 quick-drying wrinkle-resistant shirts/blouses, 2-3 pairs of pants or a skirt, optional blazer, undergarments and socks, a spare change of clothes, and comfortable shoes plus downtime slippers
assistant|business_trip_packing_list_toi: For a 3-day business trip, recommended toothbrush/toothpaste/floss, deodorant, shampoo, conditioner, body wash, razor, makeup and remover, hairbrush, contact lenses and solution, and prescription medication with documentation
assistant|business_trip_packing_list_ele: For a 3-day business trip, recommended laptop and charger, phone and charger, optional tablet or e-reader, portable charger, headphones or earbuds, and a power adapter if traveling internationally
assistant|business_trip_packing_list_bus: For a 3-day business trip, recommended a briefcase or backpack with laptop sleeve, business cards and documents, notebook and pen, calculator, and travel-sized paper clips, stapler, and tape
assistant|business_trip_packing_list_mis: For a 3-day business trip, recommended snacks, a water bottle, umbrella or raincoat if rain is forecast, sunglasses, eye mask/earplugs/neck pillow, cash and cards and ID, and travel itinerary and hotel reservation
assistant|carry_on_essentials: Recommended packing laptop and charger, phone and charger, wallet and passport, medications and prescriptions, glasses or contact lenses, a change of clothes, and travel documents in carry-on luggage
assistant|carry_on_valuables: Recommended packing jewelry, electronics such as camera or tablet, important papers, and cash and credit cards in carry-on luggage
assistant|carry_on_comfort_items: Recommended packing headphones, travel pillow or blanket, eye mask or earplugs, snacks and water, and reading material in carry-on luggage for flight comfort
assistant|checked_luggage_items: Recommended packing bulkier and less essential items in checked luggage: clothing and shoes, toiletries such as shampoo, conditioner, hair dryer, gifts or souvenirs, extra clothing, travel-sized essentials, and non-essential electronics
assistant|packing_strategy_mix_and_match: Advised packing clothes that can be mixed and matched to create multiple outfits and easily dressed up or down
assistant|packing_strategy_rolling: Advised rolling clothes instead of folding to save luggage space and reduce wrinkles
assistant|packing_strategy_wear_bulky_it: Advised wearing the heaviest or bulkiest items such as a coat or boots on the plane to save luggage space
assistant|packing_rule_345: Recommended the 3-4-5 rule: pack 3 tops, 4 bottoms, and 5 pairs of socks/undergarments as a starting point for multiple outfits
assistant|packing_outfit_target: Recommended aiming to create 3-5 outfits with the clothes brought, and packing 1-2 versatile pieces that can be worn multiple times
assistant|capsule_wardrobe_extended_trav: For extended travel, recommended a capsule wardrobe of 10-15 pieces that can be mixed and matched
assistant|packing_cube_usage: Recommended using packing cubes or small bags to organize clothes and keep them visible, and packing clothes in categories
assistant|costa_rica_usage_analysis: Noted that wearing only 3 of 7 shirts and 2 of 5 shorts on the Costa Rica trip indicates the user likely needs fewer tops and can get by with fewer bottoms
assistant|costa_rica_packing_recommendat: For Costa Rica, recommended packing 1-2 lightweight, quick-drying shirts
For Costa Rica, recommended packing 1-2 pairs of comfortable shorts or pants
For Costa Rica, recommended packing 1-2 swimsuits
For Costa Rica, recommended packing 1 lightweight rain jacket or poncho
For Costa Rica, recommended packing comfortable walking shoes or sandals along with undergarments and socks
assistant|multipurpose_packing_tip: Advised packing multitasking items, e.g., a scarf usable as a blanket, dressy accessory, or sarong
assistant|packing_list_planning_tip: Advised writing down planned activities and the clothes needed for each to identify what is essential versus not
assistant|toiletry_packing_tips: Advised decanting toiletries into smaller containers, choosing multi-purpose products, packing essentials only, keeping liquids in a clear quart-sized zip-top bag, and labeling containers
assistant|packing_tip_check_weather: Advised checking the weather forecast for the destination and packing accordingly
assistant|packing_tip_easy_iron_clothes: Advised choosing clothes that can be easily ironed or steamed to save time and effort
assistant|packing_tip_leave_extra_space: Advised leaving extra space in luggage for items that might be purchased during the trip
assistant|packing_tip_airline_restrictio: Advised checking with the airline for specific luggage restrictions and carry-on/checked size and weight limits before the trip
assistant|carry_on_tip_pack_layers: Advised packing layers in carry-on in case the plane gets cold or items must be removed for security checks
assistant|carry_on_tip_bag_choice: Advised selecting a carry-on bag that fits under the seat or overhead bin and has multiple compartments to stay organized
assistant|packing_tip_tsa_guidelines: Advised familiarizing with Transportation Security Administration (TSA) guidelines on what items are allowed in carry-on! and checked luggage
assistant|packing_tip_label_luggage: Advised clearly labeling luggage with name, address, and contact information so it can be returned if lost
assistant|packing_tip_laundry_fallback: Noted you can always do laundry or purchase items if needed, so avoid overpacking and risking a checked bag or extra luggage fees
assistant|overpacking_common_mistake: Noted overpacking is a common mistake, especially when excited about a trip or worried about not having the right clothes
assistant|packing_tip_usage_analysis: Advised analyzing what was actually worn versus what was packed as a way to refine future packing strategy
